newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission agrees beef labelling proposal.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission agrees beef labelling proposal.

text.p: The European Commission has approved a proposal by Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler for beef to be labelled to restore market confidence, an official said on Thursday.
"It's been adopted," the Commission official said.
The proposal had twice been delayed, the second time by a request from Research Commissioner Edith Cresson to use micro chip electronic identification.
The proposal, obtained by Reuters, which must be approved by farm ministers, aims to restore public confidence in beef and beef products by allowing labelling under a voluntary scheme.

"If this labelling system had been in operation prior to the BSE (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy) crisis it is unlikely that we would have seen the huge drop in beef consumption which resulted from the scare...," Fischler said in a statement.
The scheme would involve registering cows on computers and tagging them from birth.
Those wishing to label beef and beef products would have to comply with a mandatory list of descriptions restricting what can be said about a product.
Fischler is proposing two separate measures.
The first builds on existing legislation to require all animals to wear a tag in each ear, to be given passports and to be registered on central computers, the document says.
The identification system is linked to a labelling scheme for beef and beef products so that the origin of all meat can be checked.
Operators and organisations marketing beef would be allowed to label their products according to strict, mandatory rules.
Labels would only be allowed to describe the country or national region of origin, gender and method of fattening.
The proposal does not oblige operators or organisations to label beef but if they choose to do so they would be obliged to stay within the boundaries of the legislation.
